page: Microsoft Azure D64plds_v6 is an ARM-based server instance powered by a 64-core Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor running at 3.4 GHz. Built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 64 dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, eliminating hyperthreading overhead. It is configured with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 3780 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D64plds_v6 demonstrates top-tier multi-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and Geekbench multi-core metrics. Its memory subsystem achieves top-tier read and write bandwidth for large uncached blocks, reaching 465.57 GB/sec and 203.79 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and CPU physics tests also rank in the top 10%. Single-core performance, including single-threaded stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores, falls within the average range, indicating that the server's strength lies in parallelized workloads.

The ARM64 architecture and low memory-to-core ratio provide a cost-efficient profile for compute-heavy workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. The combination of high-density physical cores and fast local NVMe storage makes this instance highly suitable for multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, static web serving, and parallelized data decompression tasks.
